 Pistons could get a second chance at Naz Reid, but it won't be cheap 
 Reid is the first name in the trade rumors By Aaron Kellerstrass | Nov 17, 2026, 8:55 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Dec 16, 2022; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves center Naz Reid (11) reacts after an officials call against him on a play against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half at Paycom Center. Minnesota won 112-110. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports NBA trade rumors have already started, and the first big name being thrown around is Naz Reid, who would be a possible target for the Detroit Pistons. 
--> NBA trade rumors have already started, and the first big name being thrown around is Naz Reid, who would be a possible target for the Detroit Pistons. 
 There has been recent speculation that the Hornets will eventually trade Reid as part of their continued rebuild, and the Pistons have been mentioned as a possible destination, as they showed interest in Reid as a free agent back in 2025. 
--> There has been recent speculation that the Hornets will eventually trade Reid as part of their continued rebuild, and the Pistons have been mentioned as a possible destination, as they showed interest in Reid as a free agent back in 2025. 
 It makes sense, as Reid is just a better version of John Collins, as he’s a better defender and floor spreader who takes more of his shots from long range. He’s also on a relatively team-friendly contract that the Pistons could take on and still leave room for another possible addition. 
--> It makes sense, as Reid is just a better version of John Collins, as he’s a better defender and floor spreader who takes more of his shots from long range. He’s also on a relatively team-friendly contract that the Pistons could take on and still leave room for another possible addition. 
 There have already been some fake trades floating around that look palatable for Detroit, but they fail to take into account that there might be serious competition for Reid’s services if he does hit the trade market. 
--> There have already been some fake trades floating around that look palatable for Detroit, but they fail to take into account that there might be serious competition for Reid’s services if he does hit the trade market. 
 For the Pistons, a Naz Reid trade is all about the third part 
--> For the Pistons, a Naz Reid trade is all about the third part 
 The Pistons have an obvious trade package for Reid that would start with John Collins and an unprotected 1st-round pick. Collins’ salary almost gets you there for matching purposes, and he’s on a non-guaranteed deal past this season, so is essentially an expiring contract. 
--> The Pistons have an obvious trade package for Reid that would start with John Collins and an unprotected 1st-round pick. Collins’ salary almost gets you there for matching purposes, and he’s on a non-guaranteed deal past this season, so is essentially an expiring contract. 
 The Pistons also have control of all seven of their first-round picks and swaps, so shouldn’t have a problem giving up one pick for a proven veteran like Reid who is still in his prime and under contract at a reasonable rate. 
--> The Pistons also have control of all seven of their first-round picks and swaps, so shouldn’t have a problem giving up one pick for a proven veteran like Reid who is still in his prime and under contract at a reasonable rate. 
 The problem is that there are plenty of contenders with 1st round picks, and expiring deals, so if there are multiple teams bidding for Reid in a trade, then it might come down to what type of sweetener the team would add as that third piece. 
--> The problem is that there are plenty of contenders with 1st round picks, and expiring deals, so if there are multiple teams bidding for Reid in a trade, then it might come down to what type of sweetener the team would add as that third piece. 
 The Pistons would need at least one other salary to match anyway, but who would Charlotte want? Ron Holland II? Daniss Jenkins? Ebuka Okorie? It’s tough to say, but if some other team comes with a package that includes a promising young player, along with an expiring contract and pick, then the Pistons would likely have to increase their offer. 
--> The Pistons would need at least one other salary to match anyway, but who would Charlotte want? Ron Holland II? Daniss Jenkins? Ebuka Okorie? It’s tough to say, but if some other team comes with a package that includes a promising young player, along with an expiring contract and pick, then the Pistons would likely have to increase their offer. 
 I doubt they want to go too deep for Naz Reid, who is an upgrade, but doesn’t help their need for a second creator, so there is a line the Pistons wouldn’t cross when it came to any type of trade package. 
--> I doubt they want to go too deep for Naz Reid, who is an upgrade, but doesn’t help their need for a second creator, so there is a line the Pistons wouldn’t cross when it came to any type of trade package. 
 Reid’s salary isn’t so large that it would prevent the Pistons from getting that second creator and scorer, but it makes it more difficult if Detroit has to give up too many assets to do it.
